correctness.rationale: Given irredundant facets (a_i,b_i), for any i and c<a_i·y in projection support select z_i∈conv(S) with a_i·z_i=c. Then Q=z_i+t(P−p_i) misses y and contains every z∈S with a_i·z≤c whenever t δij≥W_j for j≠i, since a_j·(z−z_i)≤W_j. Conversely any missing translate violates at least one facet and lies in its strict-side halfspace. Taking c↑a_i·y yields exact strict formula for atomic or diffuse laws; its left-continuous projection CDF yields closed quantile halfspace depth regions. For boxes, coordinate intervals of length 2t capture all selected-side support once t≥max w_k/2; a uniform full rectangular support with query on a longest-coordinate endpoint facet has limiting depth 0 but translate depth≥1−2t/w_max>0 below that threshold, proving sharpness. Inspected rational verification source and reconstructed the geometry independently.
residual_risks: General T is sufficient but may not be optimal outside boxes; compactness is needed.
No uniform finite cutoff is claimed for nonpolyhedral bodies or unbounded laws.

value.rationale: Provides a computable exact finite-scale reduction of an infinite translate supremum to finitely many facet-direction quantiles, with atoms allowed and sharp scale for a central family. This is a useful structural theorem for robust depth regions and computational geometry, not merely a normalization of the known asymptotic depth.
residual_risks: Finite threshold depends on support and facet-point choices; optimization over p_i is not asserted.

scientific_limitations: General polytope sufficient scale not necessarily optimal, box cutoff sharp uniformly for full rectangular supports.
No unrestricted Tukey-depth identity or noncompact measure extension asserted.
